data.content: U.S. Men's National Soccer Team. # USMNT projected lineup vs Chile: Will Pochettino rotate his side? The U.S. men's national team looks to make it two wins from two in the post-World Cup era on Tuesday, Sept. 29, as it hosts Chile in St. Louis. In a match that saw 11 players earn their first caps, the USMNT beat Peru 4-1 in Orlando on Saturday, Sept. Two of those debutants, Justin Ellis and Julian Hall, scored in their first USMNT match, while Malik Tillman and Sebastian Berhalter also found the net. With a quick turnaround and two more games after the Chile match, Mauricio Pochettino will likely opt for a healthy amount of rotation on Tuesday at Energizer Park. data.content: # Devils take on the Flyers in Metropolitan Division matchup. Published Oct. 1, 2026 4:10 a.m. ET. Newark, New Jersey; Thursday, 7 p.m. EDT. LINE: Devils -168, Flyers +137; over/under is 5.5. BOTTOM LINE: The New Jersey Devils host the Philadelphia Flyers in a matchup of Metropolitan Division teams. New Jersey went 7-17-2 in Metropolitan Division games and had a 42-37-3 record overall last season. The Devils committed 254 total penalties last season, averaging 3.1 per game and serving 7.5 penalty minutes per game. Philadelphia went 43-27-12 overall and 16-13-7 in division games a season ago. The Flyers scored 240 total goals last season (37 power-play goals and seven shorthanded goals). INJURIES: Devils: Nick Bjugstad: out (pectoral), Johnathan Kovacevic: out (knee), Arseny Gritsyuk: out for season (upper-body), Seamus Casey: out (knee), Connor Brown: out (lower-body). Flyers: Helge Grans: out (lower-body), Nikita Grebenkin: out (undisclosed), Denver Barkey: out (lower-body).

data.content: # MLB Postseason Power Rankings: Strength and Weaknesses for Every Playoff Team. After Sunday’s results on the final day of the regular season, we officially know what 12 teams will be in contention for the 2026 World Series. **Biggest strength:** Elite starting pitching, lineup. The Brewers’ rotation, headlined by NL Cy Young favorite Jacob Misiorowski, has been one of MLB’s best, and it’s helped the team secure the league’s best regular-season record. The starting rotation owns MLB’s fifth-best ERA (3.65) and their bullpen has been equally impressive, ranking third in MLB with a 3.40 ERA. **Biggest strength:** Elite starting pitching. The starting rotation has been excellent, ranking third in MLB with a 3.51 ERA. The Rays hit the ninth-fewest home runs in MLB this year, and despite rostering some elite hitters such as Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz, they haven’t received much production out of the bottom third of their lineup, which is their biggest weakness with the postseason looming.
